[[Oklahoma City, OK]] }} '''Darnell Jackson''' was an [[United States|American]] [[college basketball]] player who played for the [[Kansas Jayhawks]] at the position of [[Forward (basketball)|forward]] from 2004 through 2008. He did not become a regular [[Starting lineup|starter]] until the [[2007-08 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2007-2008 season]], when he replaced [[Sasha Kaun]] in the starting lineup. Jackson, who did not begin playing basketball until the ninth grade [http://kuathletics.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jackson_darnell00.html Player Bio: Darnell Jackson :: Men's Basketball], was called one of the most improved players in the nation [http://www.athlonsports.com/college-basketball/12788/hoops-notes-emotional-season-for-kus-jackson Hoops notes: Emotional season for KU's Jackson - AthlonSports.com] for the 2007-2008 season. He attracted some attention from [[NBA]] scouts after several breakout performances, including a 25 point, 9 rebound effort against [[Boston College Eagles basketball | Boston College]]. After this performance, he was named the co-winner of the [[Phillips 66]] [[Big XII]] Player of the Week. [http://www.big12sports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/010708aaa.html Men's Basketball Weekly Honors Announced (Jan. 7) :: ] In 2005, Jackson's sophomore year, Jackson was suspended for nine games for accepting payments from Kansas booster Don Davis, a family friend. [http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=2225787 ESPN - Kansas F Jackson suspended nine games - Men's College Basketball] This was part of a rough year for him, as his grandmother had been killed by a drunk driver earlier in 2005. After scoring, Jackson often thumped his chest three times. Symbolically, one of the thumps is for Jackson's grandmother, one is for his mother, and one is for Davis. [http://www2.kusports.com/news/2006/jan/27/straight_heart/ KUsports.com - Straight from the heart] He played a big role in the Jayhawks' 2008 championship season, leading the team in rebounds and shooting percentage.
